counterfactual_missing_items: No evidence of substance use or head injury
No family history of psychiatric illness
Normal head CT and negative malaria/typhoid screens
decisive_items: A lateral flow COVID-19 antigen test and confirmatory RT-PCR were both positive
episodes of talkativeness, incoherent speech, visual and auditory hallucinations, insomnia, and grandiose and persecutory delusions
He worked as a mechanical engineer in a mining community with potential mercury exposure
response.rationale: R1 directly links confirmed COVID-19 with acute psychosis, supported by positive PCR and psychiatric symptoms, while also noting occupational mercury exposure as a potential confounder. C1 is an append-only variant of R1 with similar support but lacks the occupational exposure span. R2 has no raw support and R3 only cites exposure without confirming toxicity.

rejected.why: No raw support spans; symptoms are non-specific and acute onset with negative family history argues against schizophrenia.
Only occupational exposure is cited; no clinical or laboratory evidence of mercury toxicity, and acute psychosis with positive COVID-19 is more consistent with COVID-19 associated psychosis.
